title: Batch unsubscribe at session end with checklist review
description:
Problem: after the last swipe, the floating UndoButton (SwipeContainerView.swift:58 overlay) sits beneath the SessionCompleteView stats and can't be tapped. Undo also only covers the most recent swipe.

Design (agreed 2026-09-23):
- Left swipe records the decision locally only (SwiftData); no unsubscribe API call during the session.
- Remove per-swipe undo timer + floating UndoButton.
- SessionCompleteView lists left-swiped senders as a checklist, all checked by default; unchecking = undo.
- One 'Unsubscribe (N)' button sends all checked senders.
- Points/achievements still award at swipe time; unchecking rolls them back (reuse existing undo rollback; achievements stay sticky, streaks not reversed).
- Unconfirmed queue survives app kill; on next launch prompt 'You have N pending unsubscribes' — never auto-send.
- Show per-sender failures with retry (coordinate with e0z.9 retry queue).
acceptance_criteria: No unsubscribe is sent before the confirm tap; unchecked senders are never sent; the end screen has no overlapping/untappable controls; pending queue survives force-quit and prompts on relaunch; partial failures are shown and retryable.

title: [bug] iOS 'Run Tests' CI check is a false green
description: The iOS Build workflow's Run Tests job reports pass but runs nothing: xcodebuild errors with 'Scheme Junkpile is not currently configured for the test action', and the step carries continue-on-error: true ('Don't fail if no tests exist yet'). The Xcode project has no test target (0 'Tests' references in project.pbxproj). Every iOS PR since Feb 2026 has shown a green Run Tests check that verified nothing. Fix: add a unit test target, add it to the Junkpile scheme's test action, drop continue-on-error. Minimum worthwhile coverage: APIError.from code mapping, UserFacingError.from action mapping, and UnsubscribeOutcome.from - all pure logic, no simulator UI needed.

title: Revoke Sign in with Apple tokens on account deletion
description: Apple requires apps using Sign in with Apple to call the token revocation endpoint (POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke) when a user deletes their account (App Review 5.1.1(v), enforced since June 2022). Needs a client secret JWT signed with a Sign in with Apple private key (.p8): Apple Team ID, Key ID, and the key on Railway. The DELETE /api/account route from e0z.10 should call this after deleting local data. Also requires the iOS app to send authorizationCode on sign-in (it already does) and the server to exchange it for a refresh token to revoke later.

Apple requires working in-app account deletion for apps with account creation (App Review 5.1.1(v)). Implement: delete users row, decisions by user key, revoke Gmail refresh token at Google, return 200. Depends on 584.1 per-user decisions.

title: Enable mailto unsubscribe fallback (hasSendScope)
description: Two gaps keep mailto-only senders out of the unsubscribe flow: (1) getEmailsWithUnsubscribe filters the deck on unsubscribeData.primaryUrl, which excludes mailto (gmailService.js ~243), so mailto-only emails never appear at all; (2) hasSendScope reads credentials.scope and needs gmail.send present - the scope is requested in the web OAuth URL (server.js 625) but propagation through the mobile token-exchange path is unverified, and the doccomment still claims the getter is hardcoded false. Work: verify scope propagation end to end, include mailto-only emails in the deck, update the stale comment, and confirm App Store privacy disclosures cover sending mail on behalf of the user. (Corrected 2026-07-13: earlier description said hasSendScope was hardcoded false - it actually checks token scopes and is unit-tested.)

comments.author: Matt Snively
comments.text: Blocked on a product/privacy decision, not code. The iOS app already requests gmail.send (GoogleAuthService.swift), but the server never stores or propagates the granted scope: authTokens is built as {access_token, refresh_token} in both the Google and Apple paths, so oauth2Client.credentials.scope is undefined and hasSendScope is always false. Fixing it means the app actually sends email as the user, which needs App Store privacy disclosure and likely Google restricted-scope review. Matt to decide before implementation.

title: Unsubscribe outcome tracker: confirmed vs attempted
description: The app discards the unsubscribeResult returned by the decision endpoint (SwipeViewModel.commitPendingDecision discards the APIService.recordDecision response) and reports success for every left swipe. Add an outcome field to the Decision model (pending / confirmed / attempted / failed), populate it from the API response (confirmed = 2xx via rfc8058 or http method; attempted = request fired but not verifiable; failed = no method worked, e.g. mailto-only senders today), and surface the status wherever the app shows unsubscribes. Product decision from Matt 2026-07-13: points and XP stay the same regardless of outcome - a blocked request is not the fault of the user. The failure UX (retry / skip prompts) belongs to e0z.1.
close_reason: Merged PR 1 (c373a6a). Decisions record pending/confirmed/attempted/failed from the decision API response; session-complete card shows live breakdown; Stats gains lifetime Unsubscribe Outcomes card; points/XP untouched. Evidence: backend jest 74/74 local; CI green - iOS build 1m0s, simulator tests 4m54s, Swift/JS lint, backend Node 18+20. Manual TestFlight pass still recommended - folds into device-verify task 19b.2.

title: Optional trash of shown emails at session end
description:
On the session-end screen (from 19b.14), add a 'Also delete these emails' checkbox beside the Unsubscribe button. When checked, the confirm tap moves the email shown on each checked sender's card to Gmail Trash (messages.trash — recoverable 30 days). Scope: ONLY the shown message, not all mail from the sender (see vim follow-up for the toggle).

gmail.modify is already granted (GoogleAuthService.swift:38, server.js:593), so no new OAuth scope / Google re-verification. Needs a backend trash endpoint; APIService has no trash call today.
acceptance_criteria: With the box checked, confirming trashes exactly the shown message for each checked sender and nothing else; unchecked senders untouched; box unchecked by default; failures surfaced alongside unsubscribe failures.

title: First Step achievement icon renders as blank gray square
description:
Achievement.swift:144 maps .firstStep to SF Symbol 'foot.fill', which appears not to exist, so the badge renders empty (gray square).

Fix: use 'stairs' (SF Symbols 4, iOS 16+; app targets iOS 17). Verify every other iconName in Achievement.swift resolves too — a missing symbol fails silently.
acceptance_criteria: First Step badge shows a stair icon in Stats and the unlock toast; all achievement iconNames verified to resolve (e.g. UIImage(systemName:) != nil in a unit test).

title: Retry queue for decisions that never reached the backend
description: commitPendingDecision fires the decision API call fire-and-forget; on network failure or app kill during the undo window the decision exists in SwiftData but never reaches the backend, so the unsubscribe never executes while the app counts it as done. Add a synced flag to Decision, retry unsynced decisions on launch and network recovery, and reconcile with the outcome tracker (decisions stay pending until synced).

comments.author: Matt Snively
comments.text: e0z.1 deliberately did NOT implement the roadmap's 'unsubscribe failed -> Retry or Skip' prompt. Decisions commit asynchronously after the undo window (SwipeViewModel.commitPendingDecision), so the result arrives when the user is already several cards on - a modal at that point would break the swipe loop and the undo model. Failed outcomes are already visible in StatsView via the e0z.8 outcome tracker. The retry belongs here, as a background queue that re-sends failed decisions, not as an interruption.
